title: The creation of the UN
subject: histoire
description: The **June 26, 1945**, **51** countries sign the Charter of the United Nations in San Francisco. Born from the ashes of the Second World War, the UN wants to spare people the scourge of war.

hero.hook: After two world wars, a bold idea: force nations to speak before shooting.

blocks.text: The **June 26, 1945**, **51** countries sign the **Charter of the United Nations** in San Francisco. The objective is clear: to spare future generations the scourge of war. The UN is not a simple alliance. It wants to be a common framework for the whole world.
The project attempts to reconcile two often contradictory ideas: the equality of nations... and the real weight of the great victorious powers.

sections.title: The failure of the League of Nations

blocks.text: The idea of ​​a [[Global governance]], rules shared between states, comes from a long way away. After 1918, American President **Woodrow Wilson** launched the **League of Nations**. Based in Geneva, she wants to resolve conflicts through law. But the American Senate, attached to the [[Isolationism]], refuses to enter into it. Without the United States, the League lacks weight.

blocks.caption: The League of Nations in Geneva, fragile ancestor of the UN.

blocks.text: The League of Nations officially survived throughout World War II. It was not dissolved until **1946**, to transfer its assets to the new UN.

Without real force, without , it cannot stop Japan in Manchuria or Italy in Ethiopia. Its bankruptcy taught the founders of the UN a rule: we need the great powers within, and concrete means of pressure. [[Peacekeepers]]

sections.title: The Security Council and the veto

blocks.text: The Charter creates a two-headed structure. The **General Assembly** gives one vote to each state. The **Security Council** acts as executive body: sanctions, use of force. To keep the strongest at the table, we invented the . [[The right of veto in the Security Council]]

blocks.caption: The Security Council Chamber, the political heart of the UN.

blocks.text: Five winners from 1945 become permanent members: United States, USSR, United Kingdom, France, China. Anyone can block a resolution. Since the Cold War, the veto has often paralyzed the Council as soon as a conflict affects the interests of a bloc.

sections.title: What the UN achieves in the shadows

blocks.text: If diplomacy blocks, specialized agencies transform lives. The **WHO**, World Health Organization, coordinates global health and enabled the eradication of **smallpox** in 1980. The **UNICEF** (children), the **UNHCR** (refugees), the **UNESCO** (culture), **FAO** (food): a technical network that goes beyond borders.

Where the League of Nations had failed, the UN became essential to the functioning of the modern world: civil aviation, telecommunications, food aid, refugees. Less spectacular than the Council, this work is his real daily success.

Today, the UN has **193** members. Its 1945 structure, resulting in particular from  between Roosevelt, Churchill and Stalin, no longer reflects the world. India, Brazil, Africa are demanding veto reform. The annual budget, around **3 billion** dollars, remains insignificant compared to the ambitions. [[The Yalta Conference (February 1945)]]
The UN headquarters in New York is an international zone: clean security, clean firefighters, and even postage stamps usable only from the building.

blocks.caption: Signing of the United Nations Charter, San Francisco, 1945.

blocks.text: Created in **1945** to correct the failure of the League of Nations, the UN combines a powerful but often paralyzed Security Council and agencies whose humanitarian action changed the 20th century.
